A Dehydration System is required upstream of the HP compression stage sets to reduce the water content in the stream down to the required pipeline specification. This tri-ethylene glycol (TEG) Dehydration Systems Skid reduces the water content of the CO product gas to pipeline specification before delivering 2 it to the HP stages of the Compressor. The unit contacts process stream gas with water-absorbing TEG to remove water from the gas. The subsystem contains vendor instrumentation and a controller with an interface to the Carbon Capture main control system. The Compression Module comprises the hardware that takes the CO product stream from the 2 Regeneration Subsystem and prepares this stream for pipeline specification. The LP Compressor section has about an 8:1 compression ratio over the first three stages of the Integrally Geared Compressor to take the CO gas from about 27 psia to 210 psia. The final three HP stages of the Compressor increase pressure to 2 about 1,160 psia. while the supercritical sCO delivery system compresses the cooled gas from the HP sCO 2 2 Condenser to the conditions required for pipeline delivery. The final pressure required is ~2,215 psia.
